accuracy.evidence: Names follow NGSS 4-PS3-2 (energy carried by sound, light, heat and electric current) and 4-PS3-4 (devices convert energy), and the stored kinds (chemical, elastic, gravitational) match the KS3 energy-stores model so nothing has to be unlearned later. The torch chain is chemical → electrical → light and heat, and the old-bulb step only accepts more heat than light, matching the US Department of Energy figure that about 90% of an incandescent bulb's energy is given off as heat. Catapult range grows with the square of the stretch, as elastic store energy does (½kx²). Conservation is stated as 'never made or used up' in every place.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented ideas that energy is used up, that a bulb or battery makes energy, that only moving things have energy (the still rubber band and the book on a shelf), that a battery is full of electricity rather than a chemical store, and that devices give out only the useful output (the heat in a torch). The adult notes name each one, and the Challenge why() messages tag them as still, make, gone, back and hot.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagename is built for energy vocabulary: a stored or on-the-move sorter, a fill-the-gap torch chain with eight named energy kinds, a 10-block battery that can only be emptied into light and heat jars, a catapult whose stored elastic bar empties into a kinetic bar, and a 4-shelf drop with gravitational and kinetic bars. It passes the 30% shingle gate against all other labs and differs from flagenergy (the 14-16 skate ramp), which works with numbers in joules on one ramp.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each step makes one idea something the child does: putting a still band in Stored shows stored energy exists without motion; filling the torch gaps builds the chain of names; the blocks counter always reads Total 10, so energy cannot vanish; pulling further fills the elastic bar and sends the ball further; a higher shelf gives a bigger thump. The text after each task confirms what the child just saw.

predictions.evidence: All five teaching steps start with a locked prediction whose wrong options are the real beliefs: 'No, it is not moving' for the rubber band, 'The bulb makes it from nothing' for the torch, 'Light' or 'It vanished' for the old bulb, 'The same distance' for the catapult and 'Both the same' for the drop. The done message quotes the pick back and the lab result disproves the wrong ones.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six Challenge questions, each wrong answer tagged with a reason in why(): calling a still spring kinetic, thinking a bulb makes energy, thinking energy is used up or destroyed, thinking a flat battery refills, thinking food has no energy until you move or that only hot food has energy, and mixing stored energy with energy on the move. A rule card shows the stored and moving names above the questions.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation reads at FK grade 4.5 (family limit 5.0) with short sentences and everyday examples (toast, a drum, a book on a shelf). Adult notes read at FK 8.2 and keep curriculum codes to one sentence. Step text is two or three sentences; the energy names appear on the canvas cards so the child reads the word next to the thing.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph does a job: the kid text names stored and moving energy and the torch change; the adult text gives the curriculum link, the stored-versus-moving split, named mistakes and what each lab step shows. The family tip is an 'energy in, energy out' hunt with a touch test for warmth. The content gate found no stock phrases and explanation overlap with other lessons is under 12%.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots of all six steps in light and dark: the sort bins, torch gaps and six energy word tiles fit in three columns, jars and battery fill without overlapping labels, the shelves and bars sit side by side, and the young class gives 56 px buttons that wrap. The walk drives every task on desktop and phone.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag or tap has a labelled button twin (Stored and On the move with the card name, Next gap plus one button per energy word naming the gap, +1 Light, +1 Heat and Undo, Pull more, Pull less, Let go, Lift up, Lower, Drop it). say() writes each state into the canvas aria-label and the live caption, for example 'Battery 0 · Light 1 · Heat 9'. Energy kinds are named in text, never by colour alone. axe is clean in both themes, and reduced motion makes the flight and the fall instant.
